title: Morrow core contract version 1.1
$comment: Additions and declared replacements over urn:morrow:contracts:core:v1, which stays byte-identical. A definition resolves here first, then in v1 (docs/contracts/contract-versions.md). Replacements of v1 names are listed in changes.json.

HumanActorRef.description: A current human member acting in one workspace. Structurally an ActorRef with kind human, a workspace and a membership, and no installation or mandate.

KillSwitchControl.description: The control fields every kill switch carries (ADR-0005): a recorded reason and the agent proposal it executes, if any. A source proposal confers no authority; it is rechecked against the same tenant, capability and targets.

reason.description: Why the stop is needed. At least one non-whitespace character.

CampaignRef.description: One advertising campaign on one connection. The trusted tenant, store and connection are rechecked against the resolved record.

KillSwitchConnectionTarget.description: A store connection as the target of a KillSwitchRecord (governance.connection.disconnect, "Disconnect store"; ADR-0022 item 2 as amended 2026-10-22). v1 ResourceRef has no kind for a connection, so the record names it here: {kind: connection, id: connectionId, storeId, connectionId}, with storeId and connectionId both non-null. id equals connectionId, which validateCurrentDefinition checks in code. It is a record target only, never a grant or scope resource.

KillSwitchRecord.description: Append-only record of one executed kill switch, committed together with its effect. The owner notification is derived from it.

revision.description: Always 1: a record is never revised.

capabilityId.description: One of the five ADR-0005 kill switches.

targets.description: What the kill switch stopped: v1 ResourceRefs (a campaign, an installation, a membership or a release), or a store connection (KillSwitchConnectionTarget, the target of governance.connection.disconnect; ADR-0022 item 2 as amended 2026-10-22).

NonNegativeDecimal.description: A non-negative decimal with at most 18 integer and 6 fractional digits.

NonNegativeMoney.description: A non-negative cash amount in one currency.

RiskClass.description: Review risk class. Derived by the server from the capability effect through the fixed table in docs/contracts/review-policy-defaults.json (ADR-0011 Q9).

SelectionIndexes.description: Zero-based target indexes of a partial approval. The review library also requires them strictly increasing, in range and a strict subset.

TargetSelection.description: Selected target indexes, or null for every target of the proposal.

ProposalTarget.description: One exact change target with its own credit and cash ceilings.

ProposalDerivation.description: Marks a proposal derived by partial approval from a root proposal; its id and digest are deterministic.

Proposal.description: Proposal@2. Replaces core v1 Proposal (changes.json); not compatible with it in either direction. taskId is null only for a human-made Governance-domain proposal (ADR-0018).

taskId.description: The work task the proposal belongs to. Null only for a human-made Governance-domain proposal (ADR-0018): when it is null this schema requires a governance.* capability and a HumanActorRef proposer, and checkProposal also checks the catalogue domain and that requestedBy is the proposer. Agents always name a task.

maximumCredits.description: The sum of the target credit ceilings (BigInt).

maximumCost.description: The exact sum of the target cash ceilings in one currency, or null when every target cost is null.

irreversible.description: Equals the catalogue value for the capability; server-derived.

reviewPolicyRef.description: The workspace's single current ReviewPolicy (storeId null).

requestedBy.description: The task initiator or mandate owner; the proposer when taskId is null (ADR-0018); server-derived.

beneficiaryPrincipalIds.description: Principals who benefit from the change, such as those receiving a grant, membership or ownership; server-derived.

contextTaint.description: Derived from the evidence the proposing run consumed.

proposalDigest.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the proposal without this field.

ReviewRule.description: The review rule for one risk class.

requiredApprovals.description: Distinct eligible approvals that make a pending approval approved.

selfApproval.description: Whether a conflicted reviewer (proposer, requester or beneficiary) may approve: allowed; only a solo owner with the typed confirmation; or never.

pendingExpirySeconds.description: A pending approval expires this long after it is created.

approvedValiditySeconds.description: An approval may be dispatched for this long after it takes effect.

eligibleReviewerPrincipalIds.description: Principal IDs that may review this class, intersected with current grants; null applies no narrowing.

RestrictedReviewRule.description: A review rule for a class where self-approval is restricted (ADR-0005): never allowed.

requiredApprovals.description: Distinct eligible approvals that make a pending approval approved.

selfApproval.description: Whether a conflicted reviewer (proposer, requester or beneficiary) may approve: allowed; only a solo owner with the typed confirmation; or never.

pendingExpirySeconds.description: A pending approval expires this long after it is created.

approvedValiditySeconds.description: An approval may be dispatched for this long after it takes effect.

eligibleReviewerPrincipalIds.description: Principal IDs that may review this class, intersected with current grants; null applies no narrowing.

coolDownSeconds.description: A solo-owner approval takes effect this long after its decision.

quietPeriodSeconds.description: Solo status needs no membership change within this period.

ReviewPolicyRules.description: Rules per risk class plus the irreversible overlay, merged field by field taking the stricter value.

ReviewPolicy.description: The workspace review policy. A new revision makes approvals bound to the old one stale.

ApprovalDecision.description: One reviewer's recorded decision, idempotent per commandId.

soloOwnerConfirmation.description: Present only for a solo-owner approval: the digest of the typed phrase and the cool-down applied.

Approval.description: Approval@2. Replaces core v1 Approval (changes.json); not compatible with it in either direction.

reviewer.description: The reviewer whose decision closed the approval.

effectiveAt.description: When an approved approval may first dispatch; later than decidedAt only under a solo-owner cool-down.

ReviewDecisionInput.description: A reviewer's decision on one exact proposal digest.

expectedDecisionDigest.description: The digest of the proposal being decided: the parent, or the derived proposal for a selection.

soloOwnerConfirmation.description: The typed solo-owner confirmation phrase, compared exactly after NFC.

AccountOverview.description: GET /workspaces (P05.T01x, ADR-0009). The workspaces the signed-in person may enter now, filtered by current session eligibility in one snapshot, ordered by C collation of organization name and id, then workspace name and id; at most 100, with truncated set when more exist. onboarding is available only to a self-enrolled principal with no signup while signup is enabled for its profile. Selection is the URL /w/{workspaceId}; the server stores no active workspace.

organizationName.description: Display text only; render as text.

workspaceName.description: Display text only; render as text.

OrganizationSignupRequest.description: POST /organizations body (P05.T01x, ADR-0009): at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes of closed, duplicate-free JSON with a lowercase-UUID Idempotency-Key header. No client tenant, principal, subject or email field exists. Each name is 1-100 code points after NFC and trimming of the section 5 whitespace set W, with no code point of the control and bidirectional set F; the server applies that rule, this schema only bounds the length.

OrganizationSignupResult.description: POST /organizations result bodies (P05.T01x section 9): 201 created, 200 replayed, 400 invalid_name, 403 signup_unavailable, 409 already_onboarded or idempotency_conflict, 429 rate_limited with Retry-After: 600, and 503 outcome_unknown only after the create statement was submitted. A same-key retry is the reconciliation. 401 and other 503 replies use the fixed {code} body.

NullableId.description: An Id or null (a capability body field type; R11 needs a named type).

Boolean.description: A JSON boolean (a capability body field type).

StreamPosition.description: Opaque position, AEAD-sealed per viewer by the emitting service (P06.T02a, P07.T03). Never a decodable sequence number and never compared by clients.

PageCursor.description: Opaque page cursor, AEAD-sealed. Its decoded claims bind the principal, workspace, list kind, filter digest and issue time; another principal, workspace, list kind or filter, or an age over 24 hours, gives CURSOR_INVALID (400).

NullablePageCursor.description: The next page cursor, or null on the last page.

PageRequest.description: One page of at most 50 items after an opaque cursor, or the first page.

ConversationRef.description: Exact reference to one conversation revision.

MessageRef.description: Exact reference to one message revision.

ProjectRef.description: Exact reference to one project revision.

AccessRequestRef.description: Exact reference to one access request revision.

OperationRef.description: Exact reference to one operation revision.

KillSwitchRecordRef.description: Exact reference to one append-only KillSwitchRecord.

EventPayloadRef.description: Binds an event payload to its event: organizationId, workspaceId and storeId equal the envelope's, id is its eventId (validateCurrentDefinition checks both) and revision is always 1. digest is sha256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) payload, computed from the stored payload when the ref is built; it is not the outbox payload_digest, which hashes PostgreSQL jsonb text. A later fetch by ref resolves the tenant from the session, never from the ref.

TrustClass.description: Evidence trust class. The rank, least trusted first, is in docs/contracts/collaboration-defaults.json; P01.T02b may refine it.

CitedRef.description: The typed reference union a message part may cite (P01.T02a §9 C2). The four kind constants are distinct, so the union is discriminated by kind.

GrantVerb.description: One of the six grant verbs.

RestrictedSource.description: One view requirement: it maps 1:1 to a policy PermissionRequest {capabilityId, verb: view, resource, accountId, fields}. Sources are deduplicated by (capabilityId, resource, accountId) with fields merged; server-derived, never sent by a client.

RequestReason.description: A recorded reason: 1 to 1,024 characters, NUL-free, with at least one non-whitespace character.

ContextTaint.description: untrusted_external when any cited evidence or model-call context source is untrusted_external; server-derived.

ConversationSubject.description: What a conversation is about. One conversation per project and per task, lazily ensured by the first post. An Ask is private to ownerPrincipalId, the creating human (server-derived); workspace admins read it only through audited, read-only reads (ADR-0016 item 5).

ConversationSelector.description: Selects the conversation a post goes to.

Conversation.description: A conversation record. No status: conversations have no state machine. Positions are sealed per viewer, and posts never touch the revision or timestamps, so a hidden message leaves no signal.

revision.description: Always 1: no v1.1 command revises a conversation, and a post never changes it.

updatedAt.description: Equals createdAt; posts never change it.

lastPosition.description: The last position visible to this viewer, or null; viewer-relative.

MessageStatus.description: A human message is created completed. An agent message is created streaming by the runtime writer and ends completed, failed or cancelled; a lost lease ends it failed.

MentionTarget.description: A mention target: an active member or installation of the trusted workspace that can view the conversation subject now. Not a ref; it confers nothing.

MentionRequest.description: What the author asks of the target, under the author's own verbs: notify (an inbox item), task (a draft task, execute on workspace.task.create), delegate (an agent child task in a task conversation, delegate on workspace.task.delegate) or ask (@Morrow in a project conversation, ADR-0034 item 8). Never authority.

ArtifactPart.description: Cites one artifact revision. Adds view on workspace.artifact.read over the artifact plus the revision's recorded sources.

anchorRef.description: An anchor of the cited artifact revision, or null.

EvidenceSummaryPart.description: A summary over 1 to 50 cited evidence records. Evidence with a non-null sourceResource cannot be cited until Evidence@2 (P01.T02b) exists.

trustClass.description: The least-trusted cited evidence class; server-derived.

EvidenceSummaryPartInput.description: An evidence summary as a client sends it: the server derives trustClass.

MentionPart.description: A mention of one target: a human with notify or task, an agent with delegate, or @Morrow (the coordinator) with ask (ADR-0034 item 8). Agent-authored messages carry no mention part.

MessagePart.description: One typed message part. text and mention parts add no view requirement. ADR-0034 item 9 adds plan_card, plan_change_card and choice_question (Coordinator only), project_update and checkup_done (system author only).

MessagePartInput.description: A message part as a client sends it: evidence summaries carry no trustClass, which the server derives.

MessagePartInputs.description: 1 to 32 parts, at most 10 of them mentions; at most 64 KiB of JSON (server check).

MessageOrigin.description: Where an agent message comes from: a run in a project or task conversation (its task is the subject task or a task under the project's goal), an Ask turn, or a Coordinator turn in a project conversation (ADR-0034 items 8 and 9).

Message.description: A message. A viewer sees it only if they can view the conversation subject, hold view on workspace.conversation.post for the message fields and can view every restricted source (all-of); otherwise it is omitted from pages and counts.

position.description: Sealed per viewer; never a decodable sequence number.

author.description: A human (a HumanActorRef), an agent naming its installation with no membership, or Morrow's own code (SystemAuthor, ADR-0034 item 9); a service author is invalid.

parts.description: 0 to 32 parts (at least 1 once completed), at most 10 mentions.

replyToMessageId.description: A message in the same conversation; viewer-relative: null when the viewer cannot see it.

restrictedSources.description: Server-derived view requirements: the part requirements plus every model-call context source, deduplicated; at most 100 and 64 KiB of JSON. They only grow while streaming.

PostInput.description: A post. Restrictions, taint and trust class are server-derived, so a client cannot send them.

MessageDelta.description: A transient streaming delta, applied in sequence order. Deltas of a model call leave only after its context sources are committed and every subscriber is rechecked. A reconnect refetches the committed message and resumes at a sequence above the last seen.

StreamFrame.description: One stream frame. reset is the generic frame for a failed recheck, a resubscription or a policy-revision change; it says nothing more.

AskAdminReadAsk.description: One other member's Ask returned by an audited admin list page.

AskAdminReadRecord.description: The content-free audit record of one admin read of Asks (ADR-0016 item 5): one workspace list page, one conversation fetch or one message page. Committed in the read's transaction; content leaves only after that commit. A list record names every other member's Ask on the page in page order, each conversationId once, the reader's own left out; an empty page still gives one record. Never names the reader's own Ask (validateCurrentDefinition also checks that, and each conversationId once). Never contains message text. Retention: 365 days of content-free audit metadata.

InboxSubject.description: What an item is about; its kind equals InboxItem.kind. In a mention, conversationId and createdTaskId are viewer-relative.

StopProposalStatus.description: Derived, never stored, with precedence executed > dismissed > expired > open: executed when a KillSwitchRecord cites the proposal, dismissed when a dismissal exists, expired at expiresAt.

DecisionState.description: The decision state of an item's subject; the kind-to-machine map is fixed. Separate from read state: deciding never changes readState and marking never changes the decision.

ReadState.description: Per-recipient read state; never a decision.

InboxContext.description: Viewer-relative context: each id is null unless the viewer can view it now.

InboxItem.description: An inbox item, re-filtered at read time: returned only to its recipient, who holds view on workspace.inbox.read and can view the subject now. The owner's stop_notice is never target-filtered (ADR-0005).

recipientPrincipalId.description: The recipient, who is always the viewer.

open.description: From the fixed open-state table in docs/contracts/collaboration-defaults.json; the Inbox badge counts open items. A failed_operation exception and every informational item are never open.

InboxFilter.description: Inbox list filter; null means any. Every condition applies to the viewer-relative item: projectId matches only InboxItem.context.projectId as this viewer sees it, so a project the viewer cannot view gives the same empty page as an unknown id.

projectId.description: Matches the viewer-relative context.projectId; never the stored project of an item whose project the viewer cannot view.

InboxMarkInput.description: Marks the recipient's own items; an idempotent target state with no expectedRevision. Ids the viewer cannot see are omitted silently.

InboxItems.description: One page of at most 50 items.

ProjectTitle.description: A project title: 1 to 120 characters, NUL-free.

ProjectTabTitle.description: A project tab title: 1 to 60 characters, NUL-free.

ProjectTab.description: A tab showing the current revision of one artifact.

ProjectTabInputs.description: At most 20 tabs, in tab order; each artifactId must pass the reference rule for the writer.

Project.description: A project is a pinned Goal: a UX record over one goal, never a tenant or permission boundary. Read with goal view (view on workspace.goal.create).

pinRank.description: Viewer-relative dense rank among the pinned projects this viewer can view, from 0; null exactly when unpinned. Pins are workspace-wide, at most 20.

tabs.description: Viewer-relative: unviewable tabs are omitted; order is tab order.

AccessRequestScope.description: The authority a person asks for. Reachable only from the request input and the AccessRequest record; it never grants anything.

capabilityId.description: An existing capability that is not operator_* (server check).

AccessRequestContext.description: Where the request came from. Each id must pass the reference rule for the requester; viewer-relative on read.

AccessRequest.description: A human request for authority. Read by the requester and the deciders (eligible reviewers of the would-be governance.grants.revise proposal, never the requester). Only a linked, reviewed grant revision grants anything.

requester.description: Human only: agents have no access-request path in v1.1.

proposalRef.description: The linked governance.grants.revise proposal (P05.T02b), or null. After a partial approval it names the approved derived proposal.

decidedBy.description: The decider who denied, or the reviewer who rejected the linked proposal.

AccessRequestDecisionInput.description: A decider denies a pending request.

AccessRequestWithdrawInput.description: The requester withdraws their own pending request.

StopProposalDismissInput.description: Dismisses an open stop proposal (persisted by P11.T05). Needs execute on the proposal's kill-switch capability covering every target; an idempotent target state.

EmptyEventPayload.description: An event that carries no payload fields.

MessageCreatedPayload.description: message.created (P07.T03). Never message text; the relay reads mention rows, not the payload.

EventPayload.description: Any registered event payload: IDs and statuses only, at most 512 bytes of JCS. docs/contracts/event-registry.json binds each event type to exactly one of these, and validateEventPayload checks it.

EventEnvelope.description: EventEnvelope@2. Replaces core v1 EventEnvelope (changes.json): the v1 payloadRef is an ArtifactRef, and event payloads are not artifacts. validateCurrentDefinition also checks eventType, aggregateType and payload against the additive registry.

aggregateType.description: The registry's aggregate type for eventType.

streamPosition.description: Sealed per viewer; never the gap-free outbox position.

payload.description: The registered payload, or null for a viewer who cannot view every payload field (never a partial object).

payloadRef.description: Null exactly when payload is null, so a nulled payload leaves no digest to brute-force.

SessionRotationResult.description: POST /auth/rotate 200 body (P05.T01y, ADR-0004). rotated: a new generation was committed and its cookie (Max-Age = min(1800, floor(idleRemainingMs / 1000))) is set in the same response; current: the presented generation is younger than 60 seconds, nothing was written and no cookie is set. Remaining times are milliseconds relative to the server's delivery instant, so a client needs no wall clock: idleRemainingMs until the generation's idle expiry, absoluteRemainingMs until the family's 12-hour limit. Every refusal (denied, reuse, expired, unknown, missing or malformed cookie) is 401 with the fixed {"code":"authentication_required"} body; request-proof, body, path and method failures are 403, 400, 404 or 405 rotation_unavailable; 503 is rotation_unavailable before the statement was sent and rotation_outcome_unknown after (never retried).

ChallengeToken.description: The X-Morrow-Challenge request header (P05.T01ab, ADR-0019 item 7): one single-use Turnstile token, 1-2048 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Required on POST /auth/login and POST /organizations wherever GET /auth/challenge names a provider (staging and production). Any other shape is 403 challenge_required without a verification call; a verified request reaches its route with the header removed.

LoginChallengeConfiguration.description: GET /auth/challenge (P05.T01ab, ADR-0019 item 7): the public widget configuration for login start (actions.login) and signup (actions.signup), no-store, or {provider:none} where no challenge is asked for. The site key is public; the secret lives only in the broker.

SignInGuardOutcome.description: The sign-in abuse guard's rejections on POST /auth/login, GET /auth/workos/callback and POST /organizations (P05.T01ab, ADR-0019 items 7 and 8), answered before the route runs and before any SQL: 403 challenge_required (missing or malformed X-Morrow-Challenge, login start and signup only), 403 challenge_failed (the token did not verify) and 429 rate_limited with Retry-After: 60 (the per-address limit; signup's own per-profile 429 says Retry-After: 600). All are no-store and nothing is logged for them. A guard that cannot decide fails closed with the route's existing 503 body.

SystemStopActor.description: The system as the setter of a stop (StopRecord@1): an automatic stop such as the connection stop of the app/uninstalled webhook. It names no person.

OperatorStopActor.description: The platform operator (the owner, through an audited script) as the setter or lifter of a stop (StopRecord@1).

StopRecord.description: StopRecord@1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 15; mvp-architecture section 10; morrow_work.stop_records, migration 0020): the append-only, content-free record of one system or operator stop event, committed with its stop control. The app/uninstalled webhook writes a system record for its connection stop; the owner's audited script writes operator records for the platform stop. Human kill switches (Stop AI work, Disconnect store) write a KillSwitchRecord instead. A platform record has null tenant, store and target keys; any other record names all four, its target being the installation or connection id. Only a person lifts a stop, so a lift record is always an operator's.

ResourceRef.description: ResourceRef v1.1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 3). Replaces core v1 ResourceRef (changes.json) as a declared superset: every v1 ResourceRef is valid here. The one addition is kind store, the connected store as a whole: {kind: store, id: storeId, storeId, connectionId}, with storeId and connectionId both non-null. id equals storeId, which validateCurrentDefinition checks in code. Kernels match resources exactly, so a store resource covers only a request on that store resource.

Scope.description: Scope v1.1 (ADR-0022 item 2). Replaces core v1 Scope (changes.json) only so that resources are v1.1 ResourceRefs; a declared superset: every v1 Scope is valid here.

Grant.description: Grant v1.1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 3). Replaces core v1 Grant (changes.json) only so that its scope is the v1.1 Scope, which can name the store resource of the store-link template; a declared superset: every v1 Grant is valid here.

InstallLinkOffer.description: InstallLinkOffer (M2 PR-2; ADR-0022 items 4-5; P09.T02a): whether a workspace's connections screen offers the beta store's custom-distribution install link. offered is true exactly when url is the registered https link and reason is offered: the reader may connect (the human kernel allows governance.connection.connect administer on the workspace resource), an active app invites this workspace, its billing route is fixed to morrow_direct, and no store is linked yet. Otherwise url is null and reason names the first unmet condition, in that order of checks: linked, not_permitted, not_registered, route_not_ready.

WorkspaceConnections.description: WorkspaceConnections@1 (M2 PR-2; GET /workspace/:ws/connections): the store installations of the reader's workspace, oldest first (at most 50; StoreInstallation@1, never a credential or token), and the install-link offer. Readable by any session-eligible member of the workspace; the tenant comes only from the session.

BillingManageAction.description: The Morrow-direct purchase action of governance.billing.manage (M5 PR-1; ADR-0022 items 2 and 12): subscribe opens a Stripe Checkout session for one priced plan, billing_portal a customer portal session. The server derives it from the purchase route; it is never a request field.

NullableStripePriceKey.description: A Stripe price key (stripe:price:price_<id>, the billing v1.1 StripePriceKey pattern) or null (a capability body field type; R11 needs a named type).

ModelOptionKey.description: An opaque model-catalogue key, a model or an effort (ADR-0022 items 2 and 16): the server checks it against the active catalogue version, so adding a model, an effort or a version changes no contract.

CreditsPerProductCeiling.description: The workspace member ceiling of credits per product (ADR-0022 item 16): 1 to 99.

NullableRevision.description: A Revision or null (a capability body field type; R11 needs a named type).

AgentInstallation.description: AgentInstallation v1.1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 3; M3 PR-1). Replaces core v1 AgentInstallation (changes.json) only so that its scope is the v1.1 Scope, which can name the store resource of a store-bound installation (the Listings installation's scope is exactly its store resource); nothing else changes. A declared superset of v1: every v1 AgentInstallation is valid here, and a v1 reader refuses a store-scoped installation and so fails closed.

ModelSelection.description: ModelSelection@1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 16; M3 PR-1): the model and thinking effort of one run, or of the workspace default, as opaque catalogue keys. Closed; it never names a provider, a provider model ID, a catalogue version, a token limit or a price.

ListingProductId.description: A product of a connected Shopify store as Morrow names it (ADR-0022 item 1): product:<numeric GID tail>.

ListingFieldPath.description: One of the five listing FieldPaths of the catalog.content capabilities (ADR-0022 item 1). The set is fixed by the capability catalogue, not by a model catalogue.

ListingFieldPaths.description: A run's or a draft's listing fields: 1-5 distinct FieldPaths.

ListingSeo.description: A product's SEO title and description, as drafted: both strings (spine section 7: both are sent when either changes).

ListingTags.description: A product's tags as drafted: at most 50 distinct tags of 1-64 characters.

ListingDraft.description: ListingDraft@1 (ADR-0022 item 2; M3 PR-2): the model's proposed listing for exactly one product, the product it names and only the fields it changes. Sent to the model as the strict output schema ListingDraft_v1 (generated from this definition: every field required and nullable, no length keywords) and validated again with this definition, its HTML sanitised and its fields restricted to the run's in code. It is untrusted model output: it never names a capability, store, price or model.

ListingSnapshot.description: One product's listing fields as read from the store (spine sections 7 and 8): the content-addressed snapshot whose digest is a proposal target's expectedSourceRevision. Store content (90 days; deleted at shop/redact).

CatalogContentSet.description: The change of one product in a CatalogContentChangeSet@1: exactly the fields of its target (title, descriptionHtml, the SEO pair, tags), within the spine section 7 bounds. There is no free-text note.

CatalogContentChangeSet.description: CatalogContentChangeSet@1 (ADR-0022 item 2; spine section 7): the parameters of one catalog.content.publish Proposal@2, one item per target in target order, each the exact change of its product. Stored as the proposal's parameters artifact (emptied, digest kept, at shop/redact).

CoordinatorRoute.description: CoordinatorRoute@1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 3; M3 PR-2): the route the built-in Coordinator (deterministic code in the beta) writes for one run: ids only. Stored with its run; a model-based Coordinator writes the same record later.

ModelCall.description: ModelCall@1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 10; M3 PR-2): one call of the provider-neutral model gateway (the broker's modelRespond). Closed: it names no provider, provider model ID, model selection, catalogue version, token limit or price; the broker reads the selection and catalogue version from the run its lease names, so a call that names one fails validation before any request. It carries the merchant's request text, the run's fields and exactly one product as read, and the fence keys of the attempt (product index, attempt 1-2, sequence of a resend after a throttle).

ModelResult.description: ModelResult@1 (ADR-0022 items 2 and 10; M3 PR-2): the gateway's provider-neutral result. completed carries the structurally checked output (the caller still validates it as ListingDraft@1); incomplete, refusal, invalid_output and uncertain counted an attempt; spend_limit and provider_error end the run; not_sent (with retryAfterMs when the provider asked to wait) and input_over_cap generated nothing. It never names a provider, provider request ID, provider model ID or raw stop reason: traceRef is an opaque reference to the run manifest's call entry, where the broker records them.

ReadTagCapability.description: ADR-0031 item 6 (PR 10): the closed list of read-tag capabilities. support.case.read is the customer tag.

ReadTag.description: ReadTag@1 (ADR-0031 item 6; PR 10): a store plus one read-tag capability, computed in code (a model never sets one). The api returns a shared item only when the viewer holds view on every tag under live grants. storeId is null only for the two workspace capabilities, for an item made before any store is linked; the four store-bound capabilities always name a store.

ReadTags.description: The read tags of one shared item or run: distinct, at most 24 (a run's are the union of its tool results' tags).

DataClass.description: ADR-0031 Terms (PR 10): a read-tag capability other than the customer tag. An agent card's data classes (ADR-0037 item 4) are derived in code from its read tools.

DataClasses.description: Data classes: distinct, at most five.

CapabilityVerbs.description: One capability and the verbs a document names for it (a mandate, a package, an agent card). Names only; it is never a grant.

CapabilityVerbsList.description: Capabilities with their verbs: at most 32, each capability once (checked in code).

MandateActorRef.description: MandateActorRef@1 (ADR-0024 item 7; PR 10): the requester of a mandate run, the installation itself, fixed at admission. It carries the mandate owner so the review rules and the kernel can keep that person in the requester's place.

ownerPrincipalId.description: The mandate owner when the run was admitted; the kernel still treats this person as the requester (ADR-0024 item 7).

RunRequester.description: The requester of an agent run (ADR-0024 item 7): the person who started it, or for a mandate run the installation (MandateActorRef). Never both.

TriggerKind.description: ADR-0024 item 6 (PR 10): the kinds of server-held trigger row that admit_mandate_run takes. Mentions and assignments start a person's run, not a mandate run.

QuietHours.description: Quiet hours in the shop's time zone (ADR-0024 item 6): no mandate run is admitted between start and end (end may be earlier than start, crossing midnight). Code checks the zone against its list.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, the shop's.

MandateCaps.description: A mandate's credit caps per installation (ADR-0026 item 4's rate-card configuration; merchants may only lower them).

MandateDocument.description: MandateDocument@1 (ADR-0024 items 1 and 2; PR 10): the server-built document a person confirms with agents.installation.activate to issue or renew one installation's 90-day mandate. Bound to the actor and a standalone-workspace session, single use, 5 minutes. Code builds every field; nothing comes from the client or a model.

sessionDigest.description: The digest of the standalone-workspace session the document is bound to.

capabilities.description: The installation's grants minus human_only ones, as code built them.

expiresAt.description: At most 90 days after startsAt (a CHECK and code).

documentExpiresAt.description: Five minutes after issuedAt; the document is consumed once.

AgentTriggerSet.description: AgentTriggerSet@1 (ADR-0024 item 1; PR 10): the trigger kinds an installed agent has enabled and its quiet hours. Routines and monitors never add a kind; a mandate names a subset.

MandateTrigger.description: MandateTrigger@1 (ADR-0024 item 6; PR 10): one server-held trigger row. admit_mandate_run takes only its id; an unadmitted row stays pending and is retried at the next tick until its expiry, never dropped.

triggerKey.description: One run per trigger key (ADR-0024 item 6): a server-built key, never text.

BatchConfirmationDocument.description: BatchConfirmationDocument@1 (ADR-0024 item 9; PR 10): one typed confirmation for a solo owner's batch of 2 to 50 pending proposals of one capability and store, over their digests. It yields one approval per digest with one effectiveAt; one bad member refuses all.

phrase.description: The typed confirmation, summing the count, credits and amount.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issuedAt; single use.

ToolName.description: ADR-0027 item 3 (PR 10): the closed tool names of ToolCatalogue@1, in catalogue order. Version 2 added plan.draft (ADR-0034 item 2; PR 18); version 3 added knowledge.propose and notebook.write (PR 20). Version 4 (ADR-0037 items 1 to 3 and ADR-0041 item 24; unpublished, edited in place until it is) replaces specialist.draft with agent.propose; adds Morrow's orchestration tools agent.ask (ask or review, or a follow-up of an earlier call), agent.map, agent.message and agent.cancel; adds the memory tools memory.search, memory.read (which also opens result items, teammate results, message ranges and this context's labels, in place of agent.result.read) and memory.suggest; and adds the harness tools run.plan, run.complete (whose child form takes the place of result.submit), run.wait, result.write and context.checkpoint. knowledge.search stays for this version as an alias of memory.search's knowledge layer. A new tool is a new catalogue version and a deliberate schema change.

ToolFamily.description: read: reads Morrow or store data; internal: writes internal work records; coordination: Morrow's teammate calls, hand-offs, agent cards and plan cards; proposal: a digest-bound proposal for the gateway (ADR-0027's proposal.create family); memory (ADR-0041 items 24 and 25): memory.search, memory.read and memory.suggest, which hold no capability of their own: code decides each read per layer and target (the target's own capability over the full intersection, its read tags, its audience and the reader's live view of every source subject), and a suggestion is a message part only its requester sees, saved only by that person's tap (item 29); harness (ADR-0041 item 24): run.plan, run.complete, run.wait, result.write and context.checkpoint, which grant nothing, write only their run's own rows (with the run's audience, read tags and taint) and are checked by the lease and their closed input; computer: E2B tools under the runtime switch (none in version 4). A memory or harness tool is offered by its context, never declared by a package or picked on a card.

ToolReplayClass.description: What a tool call does after a crash (ADR-0027 item 2): a read runs again, an internal write returns its first record, a computer call answers tool_outcome_unknown.

ToolContext.description: Where a tool may be offered: the Coordinator (Morrow), a person's routed run (a hand-off), a mandate run, a look-for-work pass (reads, suggestions, memory reads and its own plan and completion; ADR-0024 item 6) or a called teammate's run (ADR-0037 item 3(a): no inbox.ask, message.post or memory.suggest, so it cannot talk to the person; it builds result items with result.write and ends with run.complete's child form, ADR-0041 item 24). Version 4 retires the specialist context with the specialist kind.

ToolWireName.description: The provider-neutral name a model sees: lower-case letters, digits and underscores.

ToolDefinition.description: One tool of ToolCatalogue@1: its family, capability and verb, replay class, 8 KiB result bound, input definition and the contexts it may be offered in. A skill never adds a tool. A memory or harness tool holds no capability (capabilityId and verb null): it grants nothing, and code decides it as its family says; every other tool names exactly one capability and verb.

inputDefinition.description: The v1.1 core definition of the tool's input.

description.description: What the model is told the tool does.

ToolCatalogue.description: ToolCatalogue@1 (ADR-0027 item 3; PR 10): the closed, generated, digest-pinned tool data in docs/contracts/tool-catalogue.json. No tool takes SQL, a URL, a role, a store, a recipient, a sender, a credential or a model, and none has an external effect.

ToolInputKnowledgeSearch.description: knowledge.search: full-text search over the shop knowledge the run may see.

ToolInputWorkRead.description: work.read: the run's own task or thread (id null), or a task, thread or artifact by id; code checks the id is in scope.

ToolInputProductsRead.description: products.read: products of the run's store by id, or whose title contains a text.

ToolInputInventoryRead.description: inventory.read: stock levels of products of the run's store.

ToolInputOrdersSummary.description: orders.summary: Level 1 order aggregates of the run's store; never a customer field.

ToolInputSupportThreadRead.description: support.thread.read: one forwarded support thread (Support only).

ToolInputMessagePost.description: message.post: a message in the run's own thread.

ToolInputInboxAsk.description: inbox.ask: a question to the run's requester; at most 2 per run, and 72 hours unanswered ends the run.

ToolInputTaskCreate.description: task.create: a task in the run's workspace, assigned to nobody.

ToolInputSuggestionCreate.description: suggestion.create: a suggestion for a person to accept or dismiss.

ToolInputReportWrite.description: report.write: a report@1 artifact on the run's task.

ToolInputAgentRoute.description: agent.route (catalogue version 4): Morrow hands work to one active teammate that must own the conversation with the person, on its own child task, with a structured brief and no character cap. Any number per job (ADR-0037 item 3(b)); it returns nothing to Morrow's run. Never in a private Ask (ADR-0041 item 33).

SkillId.description: A first-party job skill: skills/<id>/SKILL.md plus skill.json (ADR-0023 decision 11d).

OutputContractId.description: The closed list of report forms a skill may declare.

ListingChange.description: One product's listing change as a tool proposes it: every field present, null when unchanged, so the strict model schema and this definition agree. Code drops the nulls into a ListingDraft@1 and checks it again (at least one field, HTML sanitised, fields within the run's).

ToolInputProposalListing.description: proposal.listing: listing changes for products of the run's store, packed by code into digest-bound proposals for catalog.content.publish.

ToolInputProposalReply.description: proposal.reply: a reply to one support thread. Code sets every header and the sender (ADR-0030 items 3 and 10(d)); the proposal goes to support.reply.send.
