ModelProfile.description: ModelProfile@1 (ADR-0027 items 9 and 12; PR 10): a ModelSelection@1 pinned to the catalogue version it was admitted under. Never authority: it changes no tool, capability, grant, scope, rule, data class, credit cap or deadline.

ModelProfileTarget.description: Whose profile: an installation, the workspace's Coordinator, or the workspace's default for new teammates (ADR-0037 item 4: the former specialist default).

ModelProfileRevision.description: ModelProfileRevision@1 (ADR-0027 item 12; PR 10): the body of the per-agent profile command under governance.model_default.revise. The Owner may target any; an Admin installations only. Keys must be an entry the active catalogue version offers and the target's release lists.

ModelProfileChange.description: ModelProfileChange@1 (ADR-0027 item 12; PR 10): the audit and activity record of one profile change: actor, target, old and new keys and the catalogue version. No content.

AgentRunKind.description: The authority decision of every tool call depends on it (ADR-0027 item 2): routed runs (hand-offs and teammate calls, ADR-0037 item 2) use decideDelegation, mandate runs decideAutomation, the Coordinator a stated check in code. The specialist kind retired with ADR-0037.

UsdCost.description: An exact non-negative USD amount with up to 8 decimals (the numeric(20,8) of the cost tables).

AgentRunCaps.description: The caps admission pins for a loop run (ADR-0027 items 6 and 12): per turn and per run, the wall time (installed agents and the Coordinator, waits excluded) or the deadline (specialists, waits counted), and the run's hold. Checked in code, never in a prompt.

AgentRunManifest.description: AgentRunManifest@1 (ADR-0027 item 1; PR 10): what admission pins for one agent-run@1: release, system-text and tool-catalogue digests, the offered tools, the model profile and caps. Every kind runs on the wall time (ADR-0027 item 6); a routed or mandate run acts on one store and names it and its connection (ADR-0027 item 8). specDigest and dataClasses retired with the specialist kind (ADR-0037) and are always null. Code builds it from server facts; steps carry only the run id.

specDigest.description: Retired with the specialist kind (ADR-0037): always null.

dataClasses.description: Retired with the specialist kind (ADR-0037): always null.

AgentRunParams.description: AgentRunParams@1 (ADR-0027 item 1; PR 10): the Workflow parameters of agent-run@1: ids only. Everything else is read from the run's manifest under its lease.

AgentRunRefusal.description: Why admission refuses an agent run (ADR-0024 item 6, ADR-0026 item 4, ADR-0027 items 9 and 12). A proactive trigger that does not fit stays pending; a person's run is refused.

AgentRunEndReason.description: How an agent run ended. Code derives it, never model text (ADR-0027 item 1).

RunHold.description: RunHold@1 (ADR-0026 item 4, ADR-0027 item 12; PR 10): a loop run's hold, the lowest of its turn limit times its entry's worst-case turn, the US$7 backstop and its credit cap, and which one binds. A run whose hold cannot cover one worst-case turn, or two for a run that must call a tool, is refused cap_below_turn.

ModelUntrustedSource.description: The source a wrapped piece of untrusted data names (ADR-0027 item 5), and a taint kind. teammate_result and result_item: a teammate's result and an opened item (ADR-0037 item 3(a)). ADR-0041 item 34 adds notebook_entry, conversation_summary, person_memory and context_checkpoint (memory read back into a run), thread_post (a post in a shared thread) and other_member (the words of a member who is not the run's requester, ADR-0040).

ModelDataBlock.description: Untrusted content wrapped as data naming its source (ADR-0027 item 5). It never sets tools, capabilities, scope, recipients, senders or caps.

ModelToolUseBlock.description: One tool call the model made: its id, the Morrow tool name and an input in that tool's strict shape (ToolModelInput*, the schema the model is given: types, enums, required keys and closed objects, without limits). A reply outside these shapes is invalid_output and ends the run. The tool-call step validates the input again with the tool's ToolInput* definition before dispatch (ADR-0027 item 2): a limit breach is that call's invalid_input (refusal input_invalid), returned to the model within the run's tool-call caps. The broker maps names to wire names.

content.description: The result as wrapped data, at most 8 KiB (code checks the bytes).

ModelReasoningBlock.description: The model's reasoning as the provider returns it, kept only inside the run so its thinking stays valid; never shown to a person or a log.

continuity.description: Opaque provider continuity data, passed back unchanged within the run; deleted at run close.

UserModelMessage.description: The user side of one turn: the person's request, wrapped data and tool results.

AssistantModelMessage.description: The model's side of one turn: text, reasoning and at most four tool calls (code checks the count).

ModelCallV2.description: ModelCall@2 (ADR-0027 item 4; PR 10): one turn of an agent-run@1 through the provider-neutral model gateway. Closed: it names no provider, provider model id, model, effort, catalogue version, tool list, token limit or price; the broker reads the selection and tools from the run its lease names. The conversation is append-only: prefixDigest is the digest of every message but the last as the previous turn recorded it (null on turn 1), and the broker refuses prefix_mismatch before any request. final sends tool_choice none. ModelCall@1 stays for listings-run@1.

ModelTurnOutcome.description: A turn's outcome: end_turn and tool_use carry the reply; invalid_output (a reply outside the strict shapes the run was given: an unoffered tool, a wrong type, a missing or extra key, or any tool on the final turn) ends the run, while a tool_use inside them that breaks a limit of its ToolInput definition is that call's invalid_input; uncertain is booked at the worst case and sent again at most once; not_sent, input_over_cap and prefix_mismatch generated nothing.

ModelUsageV2.description: Token usage of one turn by kind, the kinds the rate card prices (ADR-0026 item 5).

ModelResultV2.description: ModelResult@2 (ADR-0027 item 4; PR 10): the gateway's provider-neutral result of one turn. message is the reply for end_turn and tool_use, and prefixDigest the digest of the conversation with it appended, which the next call names. It never names a provider, provider request or model id or raw stop reason; traceRef is an opaque reference to the run manifest's call entry.

ToolCallOutcome.description: A tool call's outcome as the model sees it (the refusal code stays in run_tool_calls). invalid_input: the input, inside the tool's strict shape, broke a limit of its ToolInput definition (refusal input_invalid); the model may call again within the run's caps.

ToolRefusalCode.description: Why code refused a tool call (ADR-0027 item 2): every check runs before dispatch and any one failing refuses it. input_invalid goes only with the outcome invalid_input; every other code with refused. PR 20 (catalogue version 3): customer_data (a run that read customer data proposes no shop knowledge) and pending_limit (a workspace holds at most 50 pending knowledge proposals). Catalogue version 4 (ADR-0037 item 3) drops route_used (no limit of one hand-off per run) and adds teammate_unavailable (not active, not on the code-built list, or the Coordinator), children_limit and insufficient_credits (kept for records written before ADR-0041: the 33rd child now checks the job in, and a first hold the wallet cannot cover parks the job, items 9 and 21), result_customer_tagged, item_not_received (an item from a result this run did not receive), page_out_of_range, hand_off_in_ask, card_tool_excluded and card_limit (10 active workspace-created agents). ADR-0041 item 34 adds parallel_limit (past a turn's tool calls; re-issued next turn), fork_first (agent.* in Morrow's main thread), retry_blocked (a dispatch over subjects with unknown outcomes), recall_out_of_scope (memory.read of a label not every part of which still passes), call_not_found and call_not_idle (agent.message, agent.cancel or a follow-up naming no call of this run, or one not idle), milestone_too_soon and checkpoint_not_requested (context.checkpoint outside a checkpoint fork); with the harness tools, plan_not_set (run.plan update or a job's run.complete before a plan), verification_failed (run.complete's gate, naming the criterion; the job continues) and item_closed (result.write to a closed item).

RunToolCallRecordRef.description: The first record an internal write made, returned again on replay. PR 20 (catalogue version 3) adds the knowledge proposal and the notebook entry. Catalogue version 4: agent.propose records an agent_card; agent.ask an agent_call (a call or a follow-up of one; teammate_run stays for records before it); agent.map an agent_map; agent.message an agent_message; agent.cancel the agent_call it acted on; memory.suggest a memory_suggestion; run.plan a run_plan_revision; run.complete a run_completion, or a called teammate's teammate_result; run.wait a run_wait; result.write the result_item; context.checkpoint the context_checkpoint.

RunTurn.description: RunTurn@1 (ADR-0027 item 7; PR 10): one row of run_turns (FORCE RLS), the only place loop content lives. No content reaches Workflow outputs, Queues or logs.

expiresAt.description: 90 days from run end (ADR-0031 item 1); reasoning blocks are deleted at run close.

RunToolCall.description: RunToolCall@1 (ADR-0027 item 7; PR 10): one row of run_tool_calls: ids, codes and digests only, never content. A refused call names its code; an invalid_input call names input_invalid. A memory or harness tool's call names no capability or verb (null): it holds none (ADR-0041 item 24); every other tool's call names the capability and verb it used, never null (the generator checks this list against the catalogue's memory and harness families).

ReportArtifact.description: report@1 (ADR-0027 item 10; PR 10): the artifact a specialist run ends with. Reports are data, never instructions; the Coordinator never reads them at launch, and code builds the parent-thread card from these typed fields.

SenderIdentityKind.description: ADR-0030 item 10(a): one kind at launch. google_mailbox, microsoft_mailbox and merchant_domain are reserved names; each enters only by its own ADR.

SenderUseScope.description: ADR-0030 item 10(e): workspace admits anyone who may approve the job. personal is reserved for linked mailboxes and enters with their ADR.

SenderDisplayName.description: A display name cleaned in code: printable, no CR, LF, quotes or angle brackets, at most 64 characters.

SenderIdentity.description: SenderIdentity@1 (ADR-0030 item 10(a); PR 10): one entry on a workspace's list of sending addresses, in sender_identities (FORCE RLS), at most one default per workspace. A launch record holds no credential. The default is always active.

SenderRefusal.description: ADR-0030 item 10(e): the identity is not active or has no adapter, or the approver may not use it. Nothing is sent.

SupportReplyParameters.description: SupportReplyParameters@1 (ADR-0030 items 4 and 10(d); PR 10): the parameters of a support.reply.send proposal, whose digest an approval binds: the sender identity id, From, To, Bcc, Reply-To, Subject, In-Reply-To, References and the plain-text body. Code sets senderIdentityId to the workspace default when the proposal is made and builds every header; no tool takes a sender and model output never sets one. Picking another sender is an edit: a new proposal.

body.description: Plain text; no HTML, attachments or tracking.

bodyDigest.description: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 body, which verification compares with the sent text.

AgentPackageKind.description: installed: an agent a shop installs or Morrow creates (either origin, ADR-0037 item 4); coordinator: the built-in morrow.coordinator release (ADR-0027 item 8). The specialist kind retired with ADR-0037.

ShopifyOptionalScope.description: ADR-0025 item 6: the optional Shopify scopes an installed agent may request at install. Nothing else at launch.

CustomerDataLevel.description: ADR-0025 item 8: none; level1 (order aggregates with no customer field, Analyst and Inventory); level2 (name and email, Support only).

SkillManifest.description: SkillManifest@1 (ADR-0023 decision 11d; PR 10): the closed skill.json beside a first-party skills/<id>/SKILL.md, pinned by its release's digest. A skill declares the tools its instructions use and the data classes it reads; it never grants a tool or a capability. eligibleForWorkspaceAgents: an agent card may pick it by id and a workspace package may pin it (ADR-0037 item 4), pinned by its digest.

AgentPackage.description: AgentPackage@1 (ADR-0023 decisions 6 and 11d, ADR-0027 items 3 and 12, ADR-0037 item 4; PR 10, generalised in ADR-0037 PR 2): one release of an agent as data, of either origin: its role text (first-party: by digest; workspace: the approved card's instructions and skill text, both bound by roleTextDigest, the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 text of {instructions, skillTexts}) and pinned skills, a workspace agent's skill text, the tools it declares, the capabilities it asks for, optional Shopify scopes, trigger kinds, customer-data level, whether it uses the computer, and the model entries it offers with its default. All agents share one tool catalogue, loop and gateway; they differ only in this. Code checks what JSON Schema cannot (agent-package.ts): every tool's capability is asked for, no package but the Coordinator's holds an agent.* tool, workspace.task.delegate or an agents.* capability, only Support asks for support.* or level 2, a workspace package holds nothing ADR-0037 item 5 excludes, asks for exactly the capabilities, verbs, scopes, customer-data level and computer flag its tools derive (item 4) and pins only skills eligible for workspace agents, and no package declares both customer reads and the computer.

instructions.description: A workspace agent's instructions (its role text), as approved on its card; null for a first-party release, whose role text is in the repository.

skillTexts.description: A workspace agent's skill text, as approved; empty for a first-party release.

AreaTemplateId.description: ADR-0033 items 6 and 7: an Everyday work area template of a first-party release, or quick_tasks, the workspace's one built-in, always-open and unmeasured Quick tasks record.

GoalKey.description: A measured goal's key, unique in its goal record (ADR-0033 item 2; flow-contracts.md).

NullableGoalKey.description: A GoalKey or null (a capability body field type; R11 needs a named type).

GoalMetricId.description: A metric of T5's catalogue offered as a goal measure at launch (ADR-0033 item 3). Its unit, direction (at least or at most), read tag and data class are fixed in code (packages/policy/src/projects/measures.ts), never by a request or a model.

GoalChecklistId.description: A checklist code counts (ADR-0033 item 3): at launch only the 12-fact Product facts complete.

GoalAssistant.description: The one AI assistant a hand check is done in (ADR-0033 item 3 and owner question 3); ChatGPT is the default. A check recorded in another assistant never counts.

GoalTarget.description: A goal's target number: finite, 0 to 1,000,000,000. Its direction is the measure's, from code.

GoalCheckItem.description: One buying question a hand check asks: Morrow writes it from shop knowledge and a person may edit it.

GoalCheckRow.description: One product row of a hand check: 1 to 10 questions.

GoalMeasure.description: How one goal is measured (ADR-0033 item 3), from closed lists: a T5 metric, a checklist code counts, or a hand check in one assistant. A goal record holds targets and dates, never a measured number.

dueAt.description: Null, or no later than the goal record's dueAt (checked in code).

startRef.description: Server-derived at read time: the goal's oldest kept goal_measure_values row. No request body carries it, and a stored goal record holds it null.

productIds.description: 0 to 20 products; none means every active product.

dueAt.description: Null, or no later than the goal record's dueAt (checked in code).

startRef.description: Server-derived at read time: the goal's oldest kept goal_measure_values row. No request body carries it, and a stored goal record holds it null.

dueAt.description: Null, or no later than the goal record's dueAt (checked in code).

startRef.description: Server-derived at read time: the goal's oldest kept goal_measure_values row. No request body carries it, and a stored goal record holds it null.

CriteriaList.description: CriteriaList, a declared superset of v1 (ADR-0033 item 2): items may add key and measure, a measured item needs its key, and at most 3 items are measured. Keys are unique in a list and a measure's dueAt is no later than its goal record's (checked in code, validateCurrentDefinition). The work API keeps its cap of 20 criteria.

GoalCriteria.description: The current CriteriaList as a capability field type (workspace.goal.revise; R11 needs a named type).

GoalObjective.description: A goal record's objective: 1 to 8192 characters, NUL-free.

NullableUtcTime.description: A UtcTime or null (a capability body field type; R11 needs a named type).

Goal.description: Goal, a declared superset of v1 (ADR-0033 items 1 and 2): one goal record behind a project, with 1 to 3 measured goals. dueAt marks a dated project, areaTemplateId an Everyday work area or Quick tasks; never both, and project commands refuse a record with neither. Writers always emit both keys.

GoalCheckAnswer.description: One hand-check answer, from a closed set (flow-contracts.md).

GoalCheckAnswers.description: The answers of one hand-check row, one per question, in question order.

GoalValueClass.description: A value's data class (ADR-0031 items 1 and 2): work (no clock), order_aggregates (90 days from its day) or customer (a customer-tagged value, on its cases' clock, stored only in a content: customer table).

GoalMeasureValue.description: GoalMeasureValue@1 (ADR-0033 item 4): one append-only value of one goal, written by code, or for a hand check by a person (workspace.goal.measure.record). Read tags, class and clock are server-derived. No model or tool writes a value.

GoalHealth.description: A health word, computed in code per viewer (ADR-0033 item 4): On track, Behind, Done (only after Finish for a project), Needs you, or Not measured.

GoalHealthReason.description: Why a health word holds; the sentence comes from a fixed template (flow-contracts.md).

GoalValueSource.description: Where a shown value comes from.

GoalMeasureProgress.description: One measured goal as one viewer may see it.

GoalProgress.description: GoalProgress@1 (ADR-0033 item 4), computed per viewer from the values that viewer may see: a goal whose values the viewer may not see is left out, never counted; the project's word uses only the goals shown. Customer-tagged values never reach it except for a viewer holding view on support.case.read, and never a project_update or the Coordinator's context.

AreaRepeatingTask.description: A repeating task an area template offers: off until a person turns it on.

EverydayAreaTemplate.description: EverydayAreaTemplate@1 (ADR-0033 item 6): closed data per first-party agent release. A person creates the area with one tap after adding the agent, at most one per template; it changes no agent package, install document or mandate.

PlanTarget.description: Where a card's records go: a new dated project, an existing project at a revision (a plan change), an Everyday work area, or Quick tasks.

PlanStepAssignee.description: Who a step goes to. A specialist step carries only a purpose: specialist.draft stays the only spec drafter.

PlanGoalDraft.description: One measured goal of a card: its measure from ADR-0033's closed lists, its startRef null.

PlanDraft.description: PlanDraft@1 (ADR-0034 item 2): the closed, digested card plan.draft posts. The model writes these fields only; code writes the values, credit range, balance, helper permissions and audience per viewer at read time. No field takes a capability, scope, grant, cap, model, recipient, sender or store.

PlanStartRecords.description: The records code computes for one start, exactly what the transaction creates under the person's own permissions.

PlanStartDocument.description: PlanStartDocument@1 (ADR-0034 item 5): built by the server on Start for the asker (or, for a code-built card, the person who opened it) on a standalone-workspace session. It binds the draft digest, the target and its revision, the records code computes, the estimate shown and a digest of the person's grant summary (never the authority). It lasts 5 minutes and is consumed once.

PlanStepRun.description: What the same tap started for one step after commit (ADR-0034 item 6): each run is admitted on its own; a refusal leaves the step Not started with its own button.

PlanStartResult.description: The answer of POST /plans/start: the created ids and each run admitted or not started.

CheckupNextStepCode.description: A closed next-step code of a report's form (ADR-0034 item 9): code writes its sentence from a template, never report text.

PlanCardPart.description: A Coordinator's card: one PlanDraft revision by id, revision and digest. Whether it was started is derived, so the message never changes.

PlanChangeCardPart.description: A Coordinator's plan-change card for a project at a revision.

ChoiceQuestionPart.description: A Coordinator's choice question (at most 2 per run, counted in code): 2 to 8 options; code adds Something else and Skip, you decide, and fills product and date pickers. Morrow sees only the tapped answer.

ProjectUpdatePart.description: The Monday project update: ids and the week only. Each viewer's copy is rendered at read time from GoalProgress@1, leaving out goals the viewer may not see and every customer-tagged value.

CheckupDonePart.description: A check-up's end: built from report@1's typed counts and closed next-step codes, never from report text.

SystemAuthor.description: Morrow's own code as a message author (ADR-0034 item 9): only for project_update and checkup_done parts, never with text or a model-written field.

CoordinatorMentionTarget.description: @Morrow (ADR-0034 item 8): the workspace's Coordinator. At launch only in project conversations; never in an Ask (MENTION_NOT_ALLOWED).

AskMentionRequest.description: Ask Morrow: the author needs execute on workspace.conversation.create and workspace.conversation.post and goal view of the project. It starts one Coordinator run with the author as requester; never authority.

PlanDraftToolTime.description: A UTC time as a tool input takes it (plan.draft; run.wait's until and a run.plan follow-through's time): UtcTime's text without the date-time format keyword, which ADR-0027 item 3 refuses in a tool input. Code maps it to a UtcTime, which is validated again.

PlanDraftToolTarget.description: PlanTarget as plan.draft takes it, flattened for strict tool use: a kind and only that kind's fields (new_project: dueAt; existing_project: projectId and goalRevision; area: areaTemplateId; quick_tasks: none); every other field null.

PlanDraftToolMeasure.description: GoalMeasure as plan.draft takes it, flattened for strict tool use: metric names metricId; checklist names checklistId and its productIds; manual names assistant, cadenceWeeks and its rows; every other field null or empty. It has no startRef: code writes it null.

PlanDraftToolGoal.description: PlanGoalDraft as plan.draft takes it: goalKey is the goal's key.

PlanDraftToolAssignee.description: PlanStepAssignee as plan.draft takes it, flattened for strict tool use: person names principalId, agent installationId, specialist only a purpose, code none; every other field null.

PlanDraftToolStep.description: PlanStepDraft as plan.draft takes it: stepKey is the step's key.

ToolInputPlanDraft.description: plan.draft (ADR-0034 item 2; ToolCatalogue@1 version 2): one card the Coordinator drafts, PlanDraft@1 flattened for strict tool use. Code maps it to PlanDraft@1 (schemaVersion 1, every startRef null) and checks PlanDraft@1's code rules; it grants nothing, creates no record but the card and is refused in a turn holding a report. No field takes a capability, scope, grant, cap, model, recipient, sender or store.

ToolModelInputPlanDraft.description: plan.draft as the model is given it: ToolInputPlanDraft's strict shape (types, enums, required keys, closed objects) without its length, range or pattern limits. The tool-call step validates the input again with ToolInputPlanDraft before dispatch; a breach is the call's invalid_input, not an invalid output.

KnowledgePageKind.description: PR 20 (shop knowledge; ADR-0031): the closed kinds of a shop knowledge page. A workspace holds at most one brand_voice page; its accepted version is the only page Listings reads, and only as marked data.

KnowledgeTitle.description: A knowledge page's title: typed text, 1 to 120 characters.

KnowledgeText.description: One version's text: typed text only, 1 to 8,000 characters (no uploads: they wait for their deletion path, P09.T05). Never customer data (ADR-0031 item 2): a page carries no customer tag.

KnowledgeSourceKind.description: Where a version's text came from: a store product, a Morrow task, or a short note a person or agent wrote (for example 'Supplier price list, October').

KnowledgeSource.description: One source of a version: a product (value product:<id>), a task (value its Id) or a note (value 1 to 200 characters). Code checks the value against its kind (packages/policy/src/knowledge).

KnowledgeSources.description: A version's sources: at most 5, distinct.

KnowledgeAuthor.description: Who wrote a version: a person (installationId null), or an installed agent (its own principal and installation) whose proposal a person accepted.

KnowledgeVersion.description: KnowledgeVersion@1 (PR 20): one version of a page, as a viewer may read it. Every version is a person's act: written by them, or an agent's proposal they accepted (acceptedByPrincipalId). Versions are append-only; deleting the page erases every version's text.

KnowledgePageSummary.description: One page in the viewer's list: the api lists a page only when the viewer holds view on every one of its read tags (ADR-0031 item 6); the tags never leave the server. It carries the current version's first 280 characters; the full text is read by its page.

excerpt.description: The first 280 characters of the current version's text.

KnowledgePage.description: KnowledgePage@1 (PR 20): one page and its current version, as a viewer may read it, with its version count. Page text is data, never instructions.

KnowledgeProposal.description: KnowledgeProposal@1 (PR 20): an installed agent's pending addition (knowledge.propose): a new page (pageId and baseVersion null) or a new version of a page made against its baseVersion. It grants nothing and changes no page; a person accepts or rejects this exact digest, and an accept of a page that changed since is stale. Only a pending proposal keeps its text. contextTaint says the run had consumed untrusted content (product text, mail, uploads or tool output), so the screen says so before a person accepts (ADR-0027 item 5).

NotebookText.description: One notebook entry: an agent's working note, 1 to 2,000 characters. Never customer data.

NotebookEntry.description: NotebookEntry@1 (PR 20): one entry of an installed agent's own notebook. People who can see the agent read it, each entry under its read tags (ADR-0031 item 6). The notebook is kept 90 days after its last write (ADR-0031 item 1) and goes with the installation.

ToolInputKnowledgePropose.description: knowledge.propose (PR 20): propose a new shop knowledge page (pageId null) or a new version of a page the run may see. It grants nothing and changes no page: a person accepts or rejects it. The server sets the read tags, the taint, the author and the page's version; a run that read customer data cannot propose.

ToolInputNotebookWrite.description: notebook.write (PR 20): one entry in the run's own installation's notebook. The server sets the installation, read tags and clock.

MemoryLayer.description: A layer memory.search may look in (ADR-0041 items 25 to 30): knowledge (approved shop knowledge pages), notebook (the agent's own notebook), person_memory (the requester's own memories, where each entry's scope allows), conversation (messages and verified summaries the requester can see), results (teammate results and result items this job received) and plan (this job's plan and its notes). Code filters by layer, audience and read tags before ranking.

ToolInputMemorySearch.description: memory.search (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 24 and 30): hybrid lexical search over the layers this run may read, up to five queries in one call. layers empty means every layer the run may read. Each hit names its source, trust class and taint; the run opens what it needs with memory.read. Results are data, never authority.

ContextLabel.description: A code label in this context's own log (ADR-0041 items 10, 13 and 14): c a tool result (c17), e an earlier checkpoint, k a knowledge page, m a message, o a gateway operation, p a proposal, q a question, r a result item, t a turn. Labels resolve only inside their context.

MemoryReadKind.description: What memory.read opens (ADR-0041 item 24): result_item (one page of an item this run received or was given), teammate_result (a call's full result, by call id, at a follow-up sequence or the latest), messages (a range of one conversation the requester can see), label (this context's own log by label), knowledge_page, notebook_entry (the agent's own notebook only), person_memory (the requester's own, where its scope allows) and conversation_summary.

MemoryReadTarget.description: The one thing memory.read opens. Code rules beyond the schema: label only for kind label; fromPosition and toPosition (from at most to) only for messages, whose id is the conversation; sequence only for teammate_result (null: the latest); id for every other kind.

ToolInputMemoryRead.description: memory.read (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 14 and 24): one page of one target, pages from 1, in place of agent.result.read, context.recall and conversation.read. Each read re-decides the target's own rule under live grants: a result re-decides the original tool's capability over the full intersection and its read tags; a message the visibility rule, redaction and other_member taint; a label refuses with recall_out_of_scope unless every part still passes; an item opens only when it belongs to a result this run received or its brief names it. What it returns is wrapped data naming its source and taint, joined to the run's.

PersonMemoryKind.description: A suggested person memory's kind (ADR-0041 item 29): a preference, a standing instruction, or a fact about the person's work. Never a special category, contact details, a customer, card or government identifier or a credential (code refuses them).

ToolInputMemorySuggest.description: memory.suggest (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 24 and 29): suggests one memory for the person this job works for, as a message part only that person sees, expiring after 30 days. Nothing is saved until that person taps Save on the exact text; never from a run that read customer data.

ToolModelInputKnowledgePropose.description: knowledge.propose as the model is given it: ToolInputKnowledgePropose's strict shape (types, enums, required keys, closed objects) without its length, range or pattern limits. The tool-call step validates the input again with ToolInputKnowledgePropose before dispatch; a breach is the call's invalid_input, not an invalid output.

ToolModelInputNotebookWrite.description: notebook.write as the model is given it: ToolInputNotebookWrite's strict shape (types, enums, required keys, closed objects) without its length, range or pattern limits. The tool-call step validates the input again with ToolInputNotebookWrite before dispatch; a breach is the call's invalid_input, not an invalid output.

TeammateRecordKind.description: The kinds of record a brief, a finding or a criterion's evidence names by id (ADR-0037 item 3(a), ADR-0041 items 19 and 29). A model-written id is never authority to read: code opens a result item only when it belongs to a result the calling Morrow run received, a person memory only when it is the requester's and its scope allows (item 29), and any other record only as the teammate's own grants, the record's read tags and the requester's visibility allow.

TeammateRecordRef.description: One record a brief or finding names.

TeammateRecordRefs.description: The records a brief or finding names: distinct, at most 256. A count bound, never a character cap: code refuses a longer list (input_invalid) and never cuts one.

TeammateBriefLines.description: Done criteria or boundaries: each a line of any length (ADR-0037 item 3, OD-2026-10-25-4: no character cap), at most 64 lines.

TeammateDoneCriteria.description: A brief's done criteria: at least one (ADR-0041 item 21), each a line of any length (OD-2026-10-25-4: no character cap), at most 64. A result reports each by its index, and a review checks each.

TeammateOutputFormat.description: What Morrow wants back (ADR-0041 item 21): the finding kinds wanted (empty: any), table columns wanted (empty: none), whether result items are expected, and how deep the summary goes. Guidance only: code builds the result's shape.

TeammateBriefMode.description: What a brief starts (ADR-0041 items 19, 21 and 22): ask, a teammate call; review, a review run checking the criteria (view verbs only, it never sees the producer's reasoning); route, a hand-off; map_batch, one batch of agent.map.

TeammateRequest.description: The requester's own words, filled by code from the message that started the job, never by the model (ADR-0041 item 21): wrapped data carrying that message's read tags. Text is never authority: authority comes from the requester in the envelope.

TeammateBriefInput.description: The brief as Morrow writes it in agent.ask, agent.route and agent.map (ADR-0037 item 3, ADR-0041 item 21): an objective, details, at least one done criterion, boundaries, the records the work is about, the output wanted and approach guidance, with no character cap (OD-2026-10-25-4); long material goes by record id. It names no tool, capability, scope, store, model or limit: code sets those from the teammate's installation and the envelope. Fields Morrow writes reach the teammate as wrapped data with Morrow's taint.

TeammateBrief.description: The brief a teammate receives (ADR-0037 item 3(a) and (b), ADR-0041 item 21): Morrow's TeammateBriefInput, plus request (the requester's own words, filled by code, never the model; null for a mandate episode, which no person's message started), mode and followUpOf from the tool input. It names no tool, capability, scope, store, model or limit.

ToolInputAgentAsk.description: agent.ask (catalogue version 4; ADR-0037 item 3(a), ADR-0041 item 21): Morrow calls one active teammate from the code-built list in its opening context, asynchronously: code admits the child in one transaction and returns {callId, state, code} at once, and the result arrives later as wrapped data (source teammate_result). mode ask does work; mode review starts a review run of that teammate's view verbs only. followUpOf reopens an idle call of this run with a new brief: the child keeps everything it read (installationId is then null). Any number per job, in sequence or in parallel; each call is one child at depth 1, admitted and checked alone. Code rules beyond the schema: installationId is non-null exactly when followUpOf is null.

AgentMapSource.description: What agent.map splits into batches (ADR-0041 item 22): record ids, or the rows of a table result item this run received. Exactly one is non-null (code); records holds at least one. A count bound, never a character cap: a larger source comes as an item's rows.

ToolInputAgentMap.description: agent.map (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 item 22): the same work over many records. Code splits the source into batches of batchSize, each one child call admitted and checked on its own with its own credits, and starts them with a warm-cache stagger; when every batch has finished, a SQL definer merges their structured parts into one result item (counts summed, created records unioned with their call ids, findings concatenated with their origin, tables unioned, failed and partial batches listed), and Morrow receives one aggregated result. briefTemplate's records are shared by every batch; code adds each batch's own.

ToolInputAgentMessage.description: agent.message (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 item 21): Morrow's guidance to one running call of this run, delivered at the child's next turn boundary as wrapped data labelled from Morrow, your lead, with Morrow's taint: never a system message, never consent. No character cap.

ToolInputAgentCancel.description: agent.cancel (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 item 21): cancels one running call of this run, or releases an idle one. Only steps that never began may be answered as not run; a step that began returns its recorded result or tool_outcome_unknown, and retry_blocked then applies to its subjects. It is not a kill switch.

AgentCardSkillText.description: One piece of skill text Morrow writes for a workspace-created agent (ADR-0037 item 4; amends ADR-0023 decision 11d for this origin only). It is instructions for that agent alone: never code, a URL or a credential, and it never adds a tool or a capability. The length bounds are provisional (ADR-0037 leaves a skill size budget open).

ToolInputAgentPropose.description: agent.propose (catalogue version 4; ADR-0037 item 4): Morrow drafts one agent card. The model writes the name, purpose, instructions and any skill text, picks first-party skills by id and tools from the catalogue, and names any trigger kinds; code derives and writes the rest (capabilities and verbs, Shopify scopes, data classes, the store, run limits, the model profile and the taint). It grants nothing: only a person's approval of the exact card does. tools is the one reviewed exception to the rule that no tool input names tools (ADR-0037 item 4: tools from the fixed catalogue); code refuses agent.*, support.*, delegation and every excluded tool.

TeammateOutcome.description: How a called teammate's run ended (ADR-0037 item 3(a), ADR-0041 item 23). The teammate chooses done, partial, nothing_found, blocked or cannot_do in run.complete's child form. Code sets partial when the run ended without run.complete but created records, wrote items or recorded findings (nothing is lost, and partial and blocked go with every end reason), and otherwise no_result, stopped (a person's stop, a switch, the lease, the envelope or the task) or failed (an invalid output or a provider error); never from model text.

TeammateCounts.description: The typed counts of ADR-0034 item 9 (what was checked, what was missing, and the questions left for a person), from which code builds checkup_done. A safety range, never a cap on work (ADR-0041 items 22 and 34): agent.map sums its batches' counts, so a large job's counts are kept whole.

TeammateFindingKind.description: A finding's type: a fact, an issue, a metric (with a value and a unit), a recommendation or a table.

TeammateTableInput.description: A table as the teammate writes it: column headings and rows of text cells. Code checks every row has one cell per column.

TeammateFindingInput.description: One typed finding as the teammate writes it, with no character cap. value and unit only for a metric, table only for a table (checked in code).

RunPlanItemKey.description: A plan item's or follow-through item's key, unique within the plan: lower-case letters, digits and underscores.

RunPlanItemStatus.description: A plan item's status (ADR-0041 item 16). Code advances items from events (a dispatched call sets in_progress, a returned result needs_review); the model sets done, blocked and dropped (a drop needs a reason); awaiting_person is set by code while a question or approval is open.

RunPlanCheckKind.description: How a done criterion is checked at run.complete (ADR-0041 item 16): record_exists, proposal_state, readback_matches (the gateway's read-back after a person's approval), artifact_schema, child_outcome, person_confirmed, or judgment (a review run's verdict).

RunPlanCriterionInput.description: One done criterion of a plan and how it is checked.

RunPlanItemInput.description: One plan item: its key, title, the indexes of the criteria it serves and the keys it depends on.

RunPlanPhaseInput.description: One phase of a plan: its title and items, in order.

RunPlanConditionKind.description: A follow-through item's typed condition (ADR-0041 item 17): a proposal decided, a proposal applied with a matching read-back, a call finished, or a time (at most the envelope's expiry).

RunPlanFollowThroughInput.description: A promise made a wait (ADR-0041 item 17): its key, title and typed condition. id names the proposal or call; at the time (UTC). Code rules: id for the proposal and call kinds, at for time, the other null.

RunPlanSetInput.description: A plan as run.plan sets it in a job's first turn (ADR-0041 item 16): an objective, done criteria with their check kinds (frozen once set), phases and items, follow-through items, and for Morrow's jobs the person-facing understood sentence and up to 6 steps, which code renders as the job's first message and the card's steps (null in every other run). No field names a tool, capability, scope, store, model, recipient or limit.

RunPlanNoteInput.description: A typed plan note with the records it cites.

RunPlanChangeKind.description: One change to a set plan (ADR-0041 item 16): item_status (done, blocked or dropped, a drop with a reason), add_item (appended to a phase; items are never deleted), add_note, add_follow_through, or change_criterion (only with the requester's message or a logged reason, which the reviewer sees).

RunPlanChange.description: One change. Code rules: item_status takes itemKey, status and evidence (reason for dropped and blocked); add_item takes phase and item; add_note takes note; add_follow_through takes followThrough; change_criterion takes criterion and reason; every other field is null (evidence empty).

ToolInputRunPlan.description: run.plan (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 16 and 24): set the job's plan (once, in its first turn), update it, or read it whole. Harness: it grants nothing and writes only this job's plan revisions. Code rules: set takes plan, update takes changes (1 to 64), read takes neither.

RunCompleteOutcome.description: How a run says it ended (ADR-0041 items 16 and 23): done, partial, nothing_found, blocked, cannot_do, or waiting (a job with follow-through items, never a called teammate).

TeammateCriterionReport.description: One done criterion as the run reports it: its index in the brief's or plan's criteria, met, not_met or unknown, and the records or items that show it. Code checks the evidence resolves to records or items the run produced or was given; otherwise the criterion becomes unverified.

TeammateNeedKind.description: What a blocked or partial teammate needs (ADR-0041 item 23): a decision, information, a grant or credits.

TeammateNeedsInput.description: What the teammate needs, with an optional question for Morrow to put.

ReviewVerdictKind.description: A review run's verdict on one criterion (ADR-0041 item 19): pass, fail or unknown. A verdict can only block; it never approves, never clears taint and never overrides a failed code check.

TeammateVerdictInput.description: A review run's verdict on one criterion, with its evidence and note.

TeammateResultInput.description: run.complete's child form (ADR-0041 item 24, in place of result.submit): what a called teammate returns to Morrow, with no character cap: a summary, counts, closed next-step codes, typed findings, what it needs, the result items it wrote and cites, and in review mode a verdict per criterion. Code adds the run's ids, the records it created (from run_tool_calls), its criteria checks, next, unresolved subjects, plan progress, verification, read tags and taint.

ToolInputRunComplete.description: run.complete (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 16, 23 and 24): the one way a job or a called teammate finishes. It succeeds only through the gate: every plan item terminal or a follow-through item, no call or question open, no unknown outcome unreconciled (with one, only partial, naming it), every typed check passing against SQL, and the review passed where it applies; otherwise verification_failed names the criterion and the job continues. Code rules: a called teammate gives result (its child form) and no reply, never waiting; Morrow's job gives reply (posted as the job's result message) and no result; other jobs give no result.

ToolInputRunWait.description: run.wait (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 item 17): one durable wait, holding no lease and no credits, for children (any or all, optionally by call id), proposals (decided, then the gateway's apply and read-back) or a time (at most the envelope's expiry). Code rules: children takes match and callIds (null: every open call of this run); proposals takes match and proposalIds; time takes until; every other field is null.

ToolInputResultWrite.description: result.write (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 22 and 24): a called teammate builds a result item across turns, so a large result is never cut: start an item (itemId null, with its title, kind and media type, and columns for a table) or append to an open one of its own, text to a text or file item or rows to a table, and close it when complete. run.complete cites items by id. Code rules: title, kind and mediaType only when starting; columns only when starting a table; text only for text and file items, rows only for tables, one cell per column.

CheckpointLine.description: One checkpoint entry and the labels it cites.

ToolInputContextCheckpoint.description: context.checkpoint (catalogue version 4; ADR-0041 items 11, 13 and 24): the model's hand-off when the fallback strategy renews a context, accepted only inside a checkpoint fork (otherwise checkpoint_not_requested). Narrative only (item 13): cite labels for the person's words, approvals, proposals and operations rather than restating them; keep ids and exact values verbatim with their labels; keep decisions and why, what was set aside, difficulties, promises and next steps. Code refuses any field that claims an approval, a consent, an apply or a payment, rejects a stated state for a proposal or operation label that differs from SQL, and runs the customer identifier screen before commit. No character cap; code checks its size against the epoch's budget.

ResultItemKind.description: text: a long summary, detail or list; table: rows under column headings; file: a text file a teammate produced. Binary files stay artifacts, named by id among the records a run created.

ResultItemMediaType.description: The closed media types of a result item's content: text only.

ResultItemRef.description: A result item as a result shows it (ADR-0037 item 3(a)): its id, kind, size, pages and title. Morrow opens it with memory.read, page by page (ADR-0041 item 24).

TaintSource.description: One untrusted source a run consumed (ADR-0027 item 5).

RunTaint.description: The taint a run, a result, an item or an agent card carries (ADR-0027 item 5, ADR-0034 item 3, ADR-0037 items 3(a) and 5, ADR-0041 item 34). Server-derived; approval never clears it, and it never truncates: kinds lists every distinct kind of source the holder consumed, sources the first 256 distinct sources, and omittedSources how many more are recorded in run_taint_sources (a join of taints adds the inputs' counts, so it may count one source twice, never fewer than there are). Code checks every listed source's kind is among kinds.

ResultItem.description: ResultItem@1 (ADR-0037 items 3(a) and 8; ADR-0041 items 22 and 24): one stored result item, a FORCE RLS record naming the run that produced it, with its read tags and taint. A called teammate builds one across turns with result.write (open until it closes it, sections counting its appends); code writes an overflow item whole and closed. Run content: on its run's run_turns clock (expiresAt 90 days from that run's end, null while it runs) and deleted with its turns.

ResultItemPageContent.description: One page of an item: a text chunk (cut at a character boundary, never inside one), or a run of table rows starting at firstRow.

ResultItemPage.description: ResultItemPage@1 (ADR-0037 item 3(a); PR 2): what memory.read returns for one page of a result item (ADR-0041 item 24), as wrapped tainting data naming source result_item. A page fits one 8 KiB tool result.

TeammateText.description: A summary or detail as a result shows it: inline when it fits, or the result item that holds it in full.

TeammateTable.description: A finding's table: inline when it fits, or the result item that holds it.

TeammateFinding.description: One typed finding as a result shows it.

TeammateCreatedRecord.description: A record the teammate's run created, from its run_tool_calls rows (code, never model text).

TeammateResultMode.description: The kind of call a result answers: ask, review (verdicts per criterion) or one agent.map batch.

TeammateNext.description: Code's hint for Morrow's next move (ADR-0041 item 23), never model text: none; follow_up (continue the same child); rebrief (once, with a corrected brief); reroute (another teammate or Morrow itself); retry_later (the provider); ask_person (a decision, information, a grant or credits); do_not_retry (stopped, or subjects with unknown outcomes).

TeammateNeeds.description: What a blocked or partial teammate needs, its question inline or as an item.

TeammateEvidence.description: A criterion's or verdict's evidence: inline record refs, or the result item holding the full list and its count.

TeammateCriterion.description: One done criterion of the brief as code checked it (ADR-0041 item 19): every criterion appears once, by index; a status the teammate did not report is unknown; met with evidence that does not resolve to records or items the run produced or was given becomes unverified (code only).

TeammateVerdict.description: A review run's verdict on one criterion (ADR-0041 item 19): it can only block.

TeammateCreated.description: The records the run created, uncapped (ADR-0041 item 19: from run_tool_calls, never model text): inline, or the result item holding the full list and its count.

TeammateUnresolvedSubject.description: A subject whose outcome is unknown (ADR-0041 item 23): the record and the operation (a gateway operation, or a computer tool call answered tool_outcome_unknown). Code refuses a retry dispatch over it with retry_blocked until the reconciler settles it.

TeammateUnresolved.description: Subjects with unknown outcomes, uncapped: inline, or the result item holding the full list and its count.

TeammatePlanProgress.description: The run's plan progress when it ended (ADR-0041 item 16).

TeammateVerification.description: Code's checks on the result (ADR-0041 item 19): criteria checks passed and failed, and the review run's overall verdict (not_run when none ran).

TeammateResult.description: TeammateResult@1 (ADR-0037 item 3(a); ADR-0041 items 19 to 23, merged by plan row H5): what one call or follow-up of a teammate returns to Morrow's job, closed and structured with no character cap (OD-2026-10-25-4): its call id and follow-up sequence, the mode, an outcome and the end reason, typed counts, the records it created (uncapped), closed next-step codes, a criterion check per done criterion, review verdicts, code's next hint, what it needs, subjects with unknown outcomes, plan progress, verification, the checkpoint it left, its read tags and taint, a summary and typed findings. Anything too large for the record (teammates.ts's bound) is a result item listed in items, so nothing is cut. Code validates it and renders a compact form for Morrow's turn as wrapped tainting data (source teammate_result); the full result opens with memory.read. One with a customer read tag never enters Morrow's context.

AgentPackageOrigin.description: ADR-0037 item 4: first_party, a release Morrow's team builds and publishes; workspace, an agent Morrow drafted as a card and a person approved. One kind, two origins.

AgentCardRunLimits.description: An installed agent's run limits as code writes them on a card (ADR-0027 item 6): turns, tool calls and questions, and the wall time. Not money: credits are the only spend limit (ADR-0037 item 6, ADR-0039).

AgentCardOwnerOnlyKind.description: ADR-0037 item 5: the four kinds of grant that need the Owner as the card's requester or approver: a store effect (an external_write capability, even with propose only), order or customer reads, spend and communication.

AgentCardDrafter.description: Who drafted a card: the Morrow run and the person whose request started it.

AgentProposal.description: AgentProposal@1 (ADR-0037 items 4 and 5; PR 2): an agent card, closed and digested with RFC 8785. The model writes the name, purpose, instructions and skill text and picks skills, tools and trigger kinds (agent.propose); code writes everything else from server facts and those tools: capabilities and verbs, Shopify scopes, data classes, customer-data level, the store, run limits (no money cap), the model profile, the Owner-only kinds and the taint. It names no code, URL or credential, and its text never adds a tool or a capability. Each person's edit is a new revision with its editor and a new digest that keeps the taint; only a person's approval of the exact digest, under ADR-0011's access-change review, creates the agent.

AddToTeamReview.description: How the request an Add to team document makes is reviewed (ADR-0037 item 5, ADR-0011 Q1 to Q3): a solo Owner with the exact phrase and the 300-second cool-down, or a second member who is not conflicted.

AddToTeamDocument.description: AddToTeamDocument@1 (ADR-0037 items 4 and 7; PR 2): the server-built document behind Add to team, bound to the card's digest and revision, the actor and a standalone-workspace session, showing the card's derived grants, scopes, data, triggers, limits, model, Owner-only kinds and taint. Valid for 5 minutes and consumed once; confirming it is the request, an access change bound to the card's digest that then passes ADR-0011's review.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issuedAt; consumed once.

AddToTeamRefusal.description: Why Add to team is refused (ADR-0037 items 4 and 5, ADR-0011 Q1 to Q3, ADR-0024 item 2). Any refusal rolls the whole transaction back.

IanaTimeZone.description: An IANA time zone name (ADR-0043 item 8). Code checks it against the closed list (packages/contracts/src/time-zones.ts), whose SQL twin is morrow_work.iana_time_zones(); a legacy alias is mapped to its zone before anything stores it.

ScheduleLocalTime.description: A local time on a 5-minute mark, 24-hour HH:MM (ADR-0043 item 7).

ScheduleLocalDate.description: A local calendar date in the schedule's zone, YYYY-MM-DD; code refuses a day the month does not have.

NullableScheduleLocalDate.description: An optional first or last local date (inclusive), or null.

ScheduleMissedRun.description: What happens to slots that fell due while nothing fired (downtime, a stop, a late cron): skip fires a slot only inside its 5-minute on-time window and drops the older ones; run_latest_once fires the latest missed slot once, inside the 24-hour replay horizon, and drops the rest. Reports use run_latest_once.

ScheduleDaily.description: Every day at up to four local times.

times.description: One to four local times, ascending and at least 15 minutes apart, also across midnight (code checks the order and the spacing).

ScheduleWeekly.description: On the given days of the week at one local time.

daysOfWeek.description: One to seven days in week order, Monday first (code checks the order).

ScheduleMonthly.description: On one day of each month at one local time.

dayOfMonth.description: A day from 1 to 28, or last (the month's last day).

ScheduleEvery.description: Every step through the local day.

everyMinutes.description: 15, 30 or 60 minutes, or 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12 hours. The slots are the local times from midnight on that step (00:00, then every step), so each step divides the day.

Schedule.description: Schedule@1 (ADR-0043 item 7; plan row SD12): one contract for mandate routines, reports and policy triggers, closed and digested with RFC 8785. Every schedule stores its zone, and its slots are local times in it. Daylight saving: a local time that does not exist fires at the next valid minute, and a repeated hour fires once, at its first occurrence. Nothing runs more often than every 15 minutes. Code-written once schedules (ADR-0043 item 9, amending ADR-0041 items 7 and 20) and standing requests on this contract (amending ADR-0040 item 12) wait for plan row SD2's dated notes, so once is not a kind here. Replaces v1 Schedule (a cron expression), which nothing stored.
